subject: Tenant connectivity: zero-trust ingress & acceptance checklist
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Emma Jones <emma.jones@curewell.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Sep 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Tenant connectivity: zero-trust ingress & acceptance checklist

Hi Emma —

Thanks again for the chat this morning. Per our call, attached are two artifacts to help accelerate the private deployment handoff: a network diagram (network-diagram-v1.pdf) and our zero-trust ingress acceptance checklist (zero-trust-ingress-checklist.xlsx).

Key asks for the intake so we can schedule a smoke/run test and baseline traffic sample:
- Confirm the egress NAT IPs or ranges you want to allow for Redwood egress (we usually request a short allowlist for control plane callbacks).
- Provide the bastion/jumpbox details (hostname, preferred admin user, port) and whether we should use SSM or an SSH key.
- Firewall rules: list the CIDR ranges and port ranges for the model endpoints (suggested baseline below).
- Certificate/KMS: confirm the customer-managed KMS key ARN and whether TLS is terminated at the load balancer or the host.
- SSO: if you want SAML auth for the console, share the IdP metadata XML and assertion consumer URL.
- Any regulatory constraints (data residency, logging retention, restricted egress) we should bake into the deployment.

Suggested baseline port list for acceptance tests (please confirm):
- HTTPS (443) from Redwood egress IPs to customer ALB
- Bastion SSH (22) from our escrow admin IPs (if allowed)
- Monitoring/metrics push (TCP 8125) to your metrics collector (optional)

Can you share the initial values by EOD Thursday? If you prefer, we can do a 30-minute technical sync — I have availability Tue/Wed next week.

Attachments: network-diagram-v1.pdf (PDF) — zero-trust-ingress-checklist.xlsx (Excel)

Thanks,
Ben
Ben Carter
Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0182

From: Emma Jones <emma.jones@curewell.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@curewell.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Sep 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Tenant connectivity: zero-trust ingress & acceptance checklist

Hi Ben —

Appreciate the clear list — this is helpful. Quick answers in-line: 
- Egress IPs: we can provide a pair of static NAT IPs (54.210.11.23, 54.210.11.24) for the short term.
- Bastion: we use a centrally-managed jump host (bastion.curewell.net). For initial testing, we can create an admin account for the Redwood team; we prefer key-based SSH.
- Ports: 443 OK; SSH (22) only from Redwood admin IPs. For endpoint traffic, we currently allow 443 and 8443 to our ALBs.
- KMS: we manage keys via AWS KMS — I'll confirm the ARN separately. TLS is terminated at the ALB.
- SSO: we'll send SAML metadata; our IdP is Okta.
- Retention: Curewell requires 12 months of audit logs and cannot export raw request payloads to third parties.

Procurement will review pricing and contract language; I'll loop them in. Attached is our contact matrix (Curewell-internal-contact-sheet.csv) with the ops and security contacts.

A couple of clarifying Qs:
1) Can Redwood provide a brief smoke test plan (sample traffic profile and expected success criteria)?
2) For zero-trust, do you expect us to provision mutual TLS certs for the ALB, or will Redwood present client certs to authenticate?

Tuesday 09:00–11:00 PT works for a sync — please propose a link.

Thanks,
Emma
Emma Jones
Senior Cloud Ops Manager, Curewell Health
emma.jones@curewell.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Tenant connectivity: zero-trust ingress & acceptance checklist

Hi Emma — quick technical note from infra: 

Summary of what we'll need to run the smoke test and an initial config proposal:
- Egress allowlist: add 54.210.11.23/32 and 54.210.11.24/32 to your ALB security groups for the test window.
- Ports: allow inbound 443 and 8443 from those IPs. We will not open SSH to the endpoint ALBs.
- Bastion access: please create a temporary admin user 'redwood-svc' and share the public SSH key; we will provide a short-lived keypair for access.
- mTLS: recommended approach — Curewell terminates TLS at the ALB and requires client cert validation. For initial acceptance we can use client certs (Redwood will provide a client cert signed by your CA) or alternate: mutual-auth via an API key over TLS. Confirm preferred method.
- Audit logs: Redwood will send anonymized request metadata to your logging collector and store request logs in the private deployment for 12 months per your retention policy — we need the S3 bucket path or logging endpoint and a role ARN if you want direct writes.

Smoke test matrix (sample):
1) Connectivity: 100 concurrent connections over 60s (HTTPS) to a test route, expect <200ms 95th pct latency and <1% error rate.
2) Prefix caching validation: confirm repeated prefix responses are cached locally (we'll run a 3k token warm-up).
3) Failover: simulate a zone outage and confirm model variant fallback within 10s.
4) Metrics: application-level metrics (success, errors, latency) must arrive in your collector within 60s.

Attachments: egress-policy.txt (sample firewall lines) — I'll push a small blueprint to the Drive folder.

If these look OK, we'll schedule a 60-minute dry-run the day before the go window to validate access and certs.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com

- On mTLS: security prefers client certs issued by our internal CA; procurement also asked to see a short SOW before signing — Ben, please share the redline and quote.

I'll accept the Tue Oct 6 09:30 PT meeting. Look forward to the dry-run plan from Karthik.

Emma
